newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis beat five Palestinians in land dispute.
newsitem.headline: Israelis beat five Palestinians in land dispute.

text.p: Israeli soldiers beat five Palestinians on Monday during scuffles over an Israeli attempt to fence off Arab-owned land in a part of Gaza under Israeli occupation, witnesses said.

They said troops guarding the Jewish settlement of Morag, near the Arab town of Khan Younis, lay on the ground pointing their rifles toward 100 Palestinian demonstrators who marched in the area demanding Israel halt the fencing.
A Reuters cameraman and a photographer were among five Palestinians who suffered bruises when soldiers attacked the crowd with metal clubs, witnesses said.
A spokesman for the Israeli authorities said the fence was to protect flower plantations belonging to Morag settlers from thieves.
Shlomo Dror, the spokesman, said Israelis and Palestinians were holding contacts about the fence. Palestinians said a meeting would take place later in the day.
Dror said the Palestinian Authority was exploiting every dispute to create tension with the Israeli side.
But Iman Dhahair, one of the land owners, said he was surprised when he found that his land and that of his neighbour had been fenced off.
"Israelis are stealing...my land. I was surprised this morning by the wire fence they erected around the area," he told Reuters.

Tensions between Israel and the Palestinian Authority have risen since Israel began a new Jewish settlement on the edge of Arab East Jerusalem in March. The construction sparked a wave of Palestinian demonstrations.
Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in clashes last year after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem's Old City.
